Vertical spacing · sentences and paragraphs

A sentence that wraps uses its paragraph’s line height; punctuation adds no extra vertical gap. Auto Pay intro: 16-unit text / 20-unit line height (4 units of leading), with 20 units below the paragraph. Offer disclaimers: 12 / 16. Shared body and helper styles use native font metrics unless a screen overrides line height; there is no universal sentence-spacing token.

List Styles & Menu Navigation

/Sparklight®

Validation Lists

Validation row spacing: 5 units below each item; 19-unit line height for wrapped text; 12-unit Radio Canada Regular in #4C5458. Row right margin: 24. Source: ChangePassword.js, bulletPoiint / bulletPointContainer.

Password requirements

  • It must be different than your username.
  • It must contain 8 to 20 characters.
  • It must include an upper and lower case letter and a number.
  • It must include at least one special character such as %, &, _, ?, #, =, -
  • Your new password cannot have any spaces.

Username requirements

  • It must contain 8 to 20 characters.
  • It must contain only letters (a-z) and numbers (0-9).
  • It must not contain any special characters (%, &, _, ?, #, =, -)
  • Your new username cannot have any spaces.

Button Styles

Primary action

Solid #8D3B90 · white label · pill radius 100.

Secondary / cancel action

Purple underlined text. The legacy SecondaryButton separately uses a gray surface and 2-unit radius.

Splash-page Login · exception

SparkLightLoginButton uses a white #FFFFFF surface and #8D3B90 bold 18-unit label on the splash gradient. Outer radius 25; label padding 16 on all sides plus 16 horizontal wrapper padding; minimum label height 48. The regular solid-purple primary-button specimen does not apply to this component.

Button States

State Example Implemented behavior
Default Solid fill; no gradient.
Pressed PrimaryButton: opacity 0.85 and scale 0.97. Base Touchable uses opacity 0.7; component overrides differ.
Disabled PrimaryButton: opacity 0.6; press disabled.
Focused Platform / assistive focus No shared custom visual focus style found in the reviewed button components. Browser focus outlines in this guide are for keyboard access.

Sizing · Component-Specific

Component / example Actual sizing rule Visual example
PrimaryButton · Continue Minimum 48; vertical padding 16; label 18. Height grows with content.
FeatureCard · Set Up Auto Pay Minimum 48; vertical padding 8; label 18; 90% width.
WelcomeCard · Get Offer Vertical padding 10; label 16; inherited 48 minimum touch target.
MobilePromo · Get Offer Minimum 44; compact minimum 40; minSize override 0.
EditActionButton · icon 44 × 44 pressable target.
Small utility action Vertical padding 4; label 14; minimum width 70; radius 2.

There is no single three-size system in the reviewed implementation. Some actions are rounded rectangles or text-only.

Selection Controls & Status

/Sparklight®

Checkboxes

Unselected

Selected

SparklightCheckBox uses a square native checkbox. Selected tint is #353091, not green. iOS sets the check and border to purple; Android uses its native selected tint. Browser examples approximate native rendering. The enclosing CheckboxRow exposes checked/disabled state and a 48-unit minimum row target.

Toggle · On / Off

Toggle.js: 36 × 20 track, 16 × 16 white thumb, green #2BA948 on, gray #4C5458 off. Visible control sits inside a 48 × 48 target. Tap either example to switch state.

Status Message Icons · On / Off

On

Enabled status pairs a green check-circle with “On”.

Off

Disabled status pairs a gray circle/check icon with “Off”, as shown in the Notifications screenshot.

Status indicators report state. They are distinct from the interactive toggle control.

Tabs & Usage Charts

Sparklight®

Service → Data Usage · Tabs

Daily UsageMonthly Usage
Daily UsageMonthly Usage

Daily is selected initially. Selecting Monthly switches to monthly usage and hides the billing-period dropdown. Only Daily exposes the date-range selector. Each tab reports its selected state to assistive technology.

ElementSpecification
Track#EAEAEA; radius 6; padding 3; bottom margin 8.
TabEqual width; minimum height 44; padding 10 vertical / 6 horizontal; radius 2.
Active#FFFFFF surface with small shadow; #353091 text.
InactiveTransparent surface; #4C5458 text. Both labels 16, weight 700.

Charts · Data Usage

25% used · 250 GB

75% remaining · 750 GB

Illustrative values

Used arc: #353091. Remaining arc: #00B8D8. Stroke: 20. Diameter: 32% of window width, clamped to 140–220. Initial fill animates over 900 ms. Pair the chart with GB amounts, percentages, billing period and remaining days; screen readers receive used and remaining values.

Charts · Historical Data Usage

Stacked bars: Download #353091, Upload #00B8D8. Daily uses day labels; Monthly uses month labels. Keep the GB axis, legend and selected-period tooltip with total / DL / UL values. Horizontal scroll reveals further periods; list view provides the same data in text. Loading and empty data use status text instead of fabricated bars.

Progress Indicators

Sparklight®

Progress indicator · steps

The app uses a segmented step indicator for walkthroughs and announcements. Document its current step and total steps rather than implying a timed percentage.

Start · step 1 of 4

In progress · step 2 of 4

Last step · step 4 of 4

PartDefinition
Active step32 × 6; #353091
Completed step6 × 6; #9CA3AF
Upcoming step6 × 6; #E5E7EB
LayoutHorizontal; gap 8; radius 3; vertically centered.

Behavior & accessible meaning

currentStep is zero-based in code; display and announce “Step 2 of 4” for currentStep = 1. The active segment moves when the step changes. Earlier segments become completed; later segments remain upcoming. The last active segment identifies the last step, not confirmation that the flow has finished.

AnnouncementProgress exposes progressbar semantics and the step label. WalkthroughProgress currently draws the segments without its own accessible label; provide the step context in the surrounding flow.

Usage is a separate measure

The circular Data Usage chart on Pg 11 measures allowance consumed. Its percentage comes from account data. Do not use the step indicator to imply download, payment or network completion; those flows need their own measured progress or loading message.

Reference & Review Notes

/Sparklight®

How to Read This Guide

This app edition follows the attached document’s section-led format: colors, typography, lists, buttons, fields, helpers, navigation and cards. Website-specific display sizes, hover/visited states and pricing cards have been replaced with app-focused examples.

HTML/SVG specimens reflect the reviewed local source; they are not native-device screenshots. Repository screenshot details are explicitly labeled and may predate current styling. Header, Account menu, dropdown and helper replacements use source-based specimens to avoid carrying forward obsolete captures.

Requested Updates

Pg 02: paragraph leading and spacing. Pg 03: validation gaps and menu-element spacing. Pg 04: splash Login exception and button sizing examples. Pg 05: border / disabled colors and corrected dropdown. Pg 07: corrected surcharge helper. Pg 08: corrected gradient order, complete bottom bar and current Account menu. Pg 09: complete Billing card. Pg 10–12: logo, icons, data-usage tabs and charts, and progress indicators.

Implementation Differences Worth Preserving

Pressed: supported, with different feedback by component. Focused: no common custom visual style verified. Links: no visited color. Lists: dashboard feature rows explicitly expose a list role. Checkbox: purple native selection, platform-specific appearance.

Button sizing: content-driven sizing and local overrides; no invented small/medium/large scale. Surcharge: inline disclosure in the reviewed payment flow; a separate due-date tooltip is implemented elsewhere.
